strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Moves crash-window recovery for MCP approval execution from process-local assumptions to Runtime-owned durable ledger convergence that external headless controllers can trigger through the existing recovery boundary.
Keeps MCP approval claim authority in durable approval state while using OS-owned advisory file locks only to serialize competing local Runtime processes.
Prevents stale MCP approval claim lock files and unfinished executing approval evidence from authorizing, blocking, or automatically retrying controlled MCP tool execution.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development, runtime_permission_enforcement, and controlled_workspace_tools by making process-loss recovery converge from Runtime durable evidence rather than lock-file existence or external supervisor judgment.
answers.new_capability: Runtime can recover after real local brownie-runtime process loss: stale residual MCP approval lock files no longer block progress, unfinished executing approvals converge to outcome_unknown exactly once, and independent Runtime processes cannot duplicate the same approval-required tools/call.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: MCP-S4.1 made approval consumption monotonic, but create_new lock files and process-local tests did not prove OS process loss, restart, durable recovery, stale-lock convergence, or two independent Runtime processes racing the same approval.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Brownie could remain permanently blocked on stale MCP claim locks or unfinished executing approval evidence after a real Runtime process loss, so real-process-loss-recovery-e2e could not close.
answers.non_duplicative: This phase changes claim locking and recovery semantics for process-loss windows; it is not another approval binding, schema, or documentation pass.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. RRP-3 uses existing mcp.tool.approve, tool.execute, task.start, and headless.run.recovery_probe boundaries, plus a test-only process-loss harness command.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The phase records bounded recovery evidence in the existing ledger and release manifests and adds an E2E test command, not a diagnostic, report, digest, history, preview, or summary endpoint.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: MCP approval claim locking now uses a standard OS-owned advisory file lock over a non-authoritative residual lock file; recovery_probe marks unfinished executing approvals outcome_unknown without replaying tools/call; and the RRP-3 process E2E proves kill/restart convergence through public Runtime JSON-RPC.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: A restarted headless controller can call the existing recovery probe after process loss and receive finite durable convergence without manual lock deletion, supervisor-owned ledger repair, or automatic retry from outcome_unknown.
answers.milestone_progress: Closes real-process-loss-recovery-e2e for the local Runtime release-readiness campaign while Runtime Release Ready remains false until durable schema migration, CI release gate hardening, protocol/event canonization, module decomposition reevaluation, platform/deadline/durability hardening, and owner license/publish decisions are handled.

implementation_audit_classification.evidence: MCP-S4.1 already exposes Runtime-owned approval admission and recomputes scoped approval fingerprints; RRP-3 reuses it unchanged in unit tests and the real-process E2E harness.

RRP-3 keeps durable approval state as authority: after inter-process lock acquisition Runtime rereads latest state, requires Approved, appends a single executing state, and denies executing/consumed/outcome_unknown reuse before tools/call.

RRP-3 replaces authority-bearing create_new lock files with OS-owned advisory file locking. Residual files remain non-authoritative and the real-process E2E proves a stale file does not block a restarted Runtime.
The public recovery probe invokes Runtime-owned unfinished MCP approval recovery and converts latest executing approval evidence to bounded outcome_unknown exactly once after restart.

Existing task/headless replay tests remain intact, and the RRP-3 process harness verifies terminal consumed state is not rerun after Runtime kill/restart while recovery checkpoint identity is validated through the public probe.

package.json exposes test:rrp3-process-loss, which builds/launches actual brownie-runtime child processes, uses a deterministic fake MCP stdio server, kills/restarts Runtime mid-call, verifies executing-to-outcome_unknown recovery/idempotence, verifies stale lock progress, verifies independent process racing launches at most one tools/call, and verifies terminal consumed state does not rerun.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: RRP-3 changes the current phase manifest and Runtime release-readiness audit while Runtime Release Ready remains false. Review must confirm real-process recovery evidence is bounded, local-runtime-only, and closes only real-process-loss-recovery-e2e without claiming full Runtime Release Ready.

exit_criteria: MCP approval claim locking uses an OS-owned advisory file lock; residual lock files are not durable authority and are not deleted for authority transfer.
Claim order remains lock acquisition, durable latest-state reread, Approved-only admission, Executing append, append success, lock release, then tools/call.
Recovery of latest executing MCP approval evidence appends outcome_unknown with bounded reason/fingerprint evidence and is idempotent.
outcome_unknown approval evidence cannot authorize tools/call replay, completion, verification success, accepted completion, permission grant, or workspace mutation authority.

test:rrp3-process-loss launches independent brownie-runtime processes, kills/restarts Runtime across stale-lock, executing-before-spawn, mid-tools/call, racing-process, and terminal-consumed windows, and verifies at most one MCP tools/call plus no duplicate terminal recovery evidence.
behavior_evidence: brownie-runtime mcp_tool_stale_claim_lock_file_does_not_authorize_or_block_claim covers residual lock-file non-authority and stale-file progress under OS advisory locking.

brownie-runtime mcp_tool_recovery_probe_marks_unfinished_executing_once_and_blocks_reuse covers executing to outcome_unknown recovery, idempotence, bounded recovery fingerprint evidence, and reuse denial.

test:rrp3-process-loss covers actual brownie-runtime process kill/restart, stale residual lock progress, executing-before-spawn recovery, mid-tools/call outcome_unknown recovery, independent process racing with at most one tools/call, and terminal consumed state non-rerun after restart.
Existing MCP approval tests continue to cover consumed reuse denial, concurrent same-approval single tools/call, timeout outcome_unknown, and key_required fail-closed behavior.

accepted_capability: MCP approval claim locks are no longer permanent authority-bearing create_new files.
Unfinished executing MCP approval state converges to outcome_unknown through Runtime-owned recovery.
Real local brownie-runtime process loss and independent process racing are covered by a dedicated E2E command.
behavior_evidence: Focused runtime tests cover stale residual lock files, executing recovery idempotence, and no tools/call replay from outcome_unknown.
test:rrp3-process-loss launches/kills/restarts real runtime child processes through public JSON-RPC and verifies durable convergence plus at-most-once fake MCP tools/call evidence.
safety_boundary: Rust Runtime remains the execution, admission, replay, ledger, permission, recovery, and tool authority.
CLI and VSIX remain thin transport/projection/validation layers.
MCP approval state and recovery evidence are narrowing-only and cannot grant authority.
non_goals: Does not claim Runtime Release Ready.
Does not start durable schema migration, CI workflow hardening, protocol/event canonization, module decomposition, platform/deadline/durability hardening, or OSS license/publish work.
Does not add scheduler, daemon, hosted supervisor, generic shell, arbitrary process execution, package distribution, or signing infrastructure.
rejected_alternatives: Rejected using lock-file existence or deletion as authority because durable MCP approval state remains the Runtime-owned source of truth.
Rejected PID-age or timeout-only stale-lock takeover because local Runtime v0 can rely on OS-owned advisory file lock release after process loss while treating residual files as non-authoritative.
Rejected automatically retrying tools/call from outcome_unknown because external MCP side effects may already have occurred before Runtime process loss.
Rejected placing recovery responsibility in CLI, VSIX, an external supervisor, or manual operator cleanup because RRP-3 requires recovery through public Runtime boundaries.
technical_debt: Remaining post-RRP-3 blockers stay open until separately authorized.
next_capability_rationale: After RRP-3 lands, stop as requested and leave durable schema migration, CI release gate hardening, protocol/event canonization, runtime module decomposition reevaluation, platform/deadline/durability hardening, and OSS license/publish decisions for separately authorized phases.

runtime_release_dod: RRP-3 closes the Runtime-owned local real process-loss recovery E2E blocker for MCP approval claim locks, executing approval recovery, durable ledger convergence, and at-most-once tools/call evidence.
Runtime Release Ready remains false until the remaining runtime P0/P1 blockers and owner license/publish decision are resolved.
runtime_boundary_contracts: Recovery is exercised through existing public Runtime JSON-RPC boundaries including task.start, mcp.tool.approve, tool.execute, and headless.run.recovery_probe.
CLI and VSIX remain thin transport/projection layers over Runtime-owned contracts.
external_control_plane_responsibilities: External scheduling, queueing, worker leases, hosted isolation, retry policy, metrics, alerts, SLA, tenant administration, billing, and secret-provider operations remain outside this local Runtime v0 phase.
No external controller gains authority to decide MCP approval claim, replay, completion, or recovery state.
external_adapter_responsibilities: Forge, pull request, review, notification, SIEM, OTel, language verifier, customer integration, and hosted MCP adapter responsibilities remain outside RRP-3.
No external adapter is required to manually delete locks or directly mutate Runtime ledger state.
commercial_solution_readiness: Packaging, distribution, signing, notarization, enterprise administration, operational runbooks, support, and commercial release decisions remain out of scope.
Cargo license and publish settings remain owner-decision items and are not changed by RRP-3.
